summary: This Dockerfile builds a .NET application in a temporary stage, then creates a final lightweight runtime image that includes the compiled application and Oracle database client libraries needed to connect to Oracle databases. It uses a multi-stage build to keep the final image small by discarding the build tools.

explanations.3: This starts with Microsoft's .NET SDK image version 8.0 and labels this stage as 'build' — we'll use it to compile code, then throw it away later.
explanations.7: Copy only the project file (.csproj) first, before copying source code, so Docker can cache the dependency download step separately from code changes.
explanations.8: Download and cache all the NuGet packages this project needs — doing this before copying the full source lets Docker reuse this layer if only code (not dependencies) changed.
explanations.13: Switch to a much smaller runtime-only image for the final container — we don't need the compiler anymore, just the .NET runtime to execute the already-built application.
explanations.17: Copy the compiled application output from the 'build' stage into the final image — this is the actual .dll file that will run.
explanations.20: Define a variable for the Oracle client version number so you can change it in one place without editing the whole file.
explanations.23: Install system packages needed to download and unzip the Oracle client; the 'no-install-recommends' and cleanup afterward keep the image small.
explanations.29: Download Oracle's client library as a zip file, extract it to a standard system location, create symbolic links so the application can find the libraries, and update the system's library cache so the OS knows where to find them.
